newsitem.title: USA: SBC and PacTel access lines grew in Q1.
newsitem.headline: SBC and PacTel access lines grew in Q1.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc, which completed its acquisition of Pacific Telesis Group on April 1, on Thursday reported first quarter results for each company showing continued growth in lines to customers.
SBC access lines rose 5.1 percent year on year while Pactel lines rose 3.9 percent. Business lines, included in the total, grew 8.5 percent at SBC and 4.7 percent at PacTel.
The results are the last before the company reports combined proforma first quarter results on May 9 which are expected to include more details.

On a standalone basis SBC reported a 13.2 percent increase in first quarter earnings per share to $0.86 per share from $0.76 a year earlier. PacTel earnings per share fell 17.6 percent to $0.61 from $0.74 a year ago, before gains.

The weaker Pactel earnings were attributed to start-up costs for new initiatives, mainly digital Personal Communications Services (PCS), the costs of preparing for competition in local telephone and winter storm damage costs.
The company declined to break down those figures between categories, or put a figure on the total effect, before the combined figures to be released in May.
SBC wireless customers increased by 21.7 percent year on year to 4.66 million, while PacTel -- which is just launching PCS services -- gained 25,000 customers in the quarter.
PacTel's original cellular operations were spun off with AirTouch Communications Inc in April 1994.
Edward Whitacre, chief executive of the combined company said he was pleased with the results of both regional Bells.

"Operating fundamentals across SBC's businesses and regions continue to reflect strong growth trends in access lines and demand for data-related appalications...," he said. (( -- Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
